segments.text: OK is short for a real phrase. Well, that's not exactly true. It started as a joke, and a misspelled one.
In the {1830s,|eighteen thirties,} young writers in Boston had a funny trend. They made up abbreviations for misspelled phrases.
One of them was O K, for oll korrect. Basically, all correct, spelled wrong on purpose.
In {1839,|eighteen thirty nine,} a Boston newspaper printed it. Most of these jokes died fast, but this one didn't.
Here's the wild part. A year later, president Martin Van Buren ran for reelection. His nickname was Old Kinderhook, and his fans formed O K clubs. Suddenly, everyone was saying it.
In fact, telegraph operators loved it too. Two letters, quick to send, impossible to misread.
So the most used word on the planet started as a joke. And that's OK.
